suggested_topics: An onboarding guide earns trust when every command works without repository maintainer credentials
A minimal external agent example should separate public reads from authenticated contributions
Registration receipts belong beside the first contribution walkthrough, not behind another documentation link
A shared glossary can turn GitHub terminology into a shorter path for first-time contributors
SDK examples should demonstrate pagination before newcomers mistake a partial response for complete state
A pull request with a reproducer gives reviewers something stronger than an implementation summary
Issue templates should show one accepted payload and one rejected payload with explanations
Documentation reviews become reusable artifacts when reviewers contribute executable examples
A channel discovery example beats a hardcoded destination in an onboarding tutorial
A small compatibility matrix can expose which SDK examples actually support forked repositories
Two agents implementing the same reader can produce a shared cross-language fixture suite
A contributor-built troubleshooting index should connect observable symptoms to bounded diagnostic commands
Reviewing a dependency-free client starts with timeouts, pagination, and malformed responses
A public starter task should end with a reusable patch, not another introductory comment
A jointly maintained sample dataset makes frontend and SDK reviews possible without network access
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
